# ECN-2026-019 - Change notice - Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01

Reason for change
- Background: Routine audits and operator feedback identified variability in surface quality of ring-rolled components processed in the Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet identified as EQ-P3-L2-SB01. Inspection records and process reviews indicated that media wear and contamination were contributing factors influencing blast effectiveness and repeatability.
- Purpose: This change updates the preventive maintenance practice specific to shot media replenishment for EQ-P3-L2-SB01 to improve consistency of blast results, reduce rework, and align maintenance activity with actual process demands while minimizing production interruptions.
- Root cause rationale: Analysis showed that media degradation and gradual size distribution shift reduce kinetic efficiency and change abrasive behavior over time. Top-up frequency was observed to lag behind the rate of effective media loss and contamination accumulation. Adjusting the media top-up cadence addresses the root cause by restoring media mass and abrasive profile before process drift becomes measurable.

Affected items
- Equipment affected: EQ-P3-L2-SB01 (Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1) only. No changes to other shot blast cabinets or different processes in plant P3 are covered by this ECN.
- Procedures impacted: Operators and maintenance personnel shall follow updated instructions and recordkeeping practices in SOP-P3-L2-02, SOP-P3-L2-03, and SOP-P3-L2-05 where those procedures reference shot media handling, cabinet operation, and quality acceptance criteria. Cross-reference check: these SOPs remain the governing documents for routine operation and quality checks; this ECN modifies how often media is topped up for the listed equipment and documents required to capture.
- Spare parts and consumables: Existing approved shot media type and vendor remain unchanged. This ECN does not change material specifications or introduce new consumables.

Implementation
- Change detail: The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours. This interval is the new standard cadence for adding fresh shot media to the cabinet hopper to maintain target media mass and abrasive performance between scheduled full media maintenance events.
- Implementation steps:
  - Supervisors will update the maintenance schedule in the local planning board and electronic maintenance system to reflect the new top-up cadence for EQ-P3-L2-SB01.
  - Operators will perform a media level and contamination check at shift turnover and log the check in the cabinet log. If media shows abnormal contamination or degradation outside expected conditions, escalate per SOP-P3-L2-03.
  - Maintenance technicians will perform the media top-up action per the cabinet handling instructions in SOP-P3-L2-02. Top-up actions will replenish media to the nominal fill point specified in existing cabinet documentation; no change to fill point is authorized by this ECN.
  - Quality engineering will sample processed parts at normal inspection gates and track surface uniformity trends for a baseline period following implementation to confirm effectiveness.
- Examples and acceptance criteria:
  - Example scenario: If, during a production run, an operator notes increased dusting or reduced finish uniformity, the operator will document the observation and perform the prescribed media check. If the observation correlates to media level below acceptable visual range or visible contamination, a top-up action in accordance with the new interval statement will be executed immediately and recorded.
  - Acceptance criteria: Post-implementation data should show reduced incidence of rework related to surface finish, stable inspection metrics, and reduced variance in acceptance decisions at quality gates. Any deviation will trigger a review and possible adjustment in execution fidelity rather than further change to hours interval.
- Records to keep:
  - Cabinet media log entries for EQ-P3-L2-SB01 showing date, shift, operator initials, media top-up confirmation, and any noted anomalies.
  - Maintenance service call records and work orders referencing the top-up action and linking to the cabinet log.
  - Quality inspection records and trend analysis reports for the ring-rolled product family processed through EQ-P3-L2-SB01, maintained per plant retention policy and referenced in follow-up reviews.
- Training and communication:
  - Operators, maintenance, and quality personnel assigned to P3-L2 will receive briefing on the top-up interval change and the required log practices. Briefing materials will reference SOP-P3-L2-02, SOP-P3-L2-03, and SOP-P3-L2-05 for operational and quality criteria.
  - Supervisors are responsible for ensuring briefing completion and for initial verification of record entries for a monitoring period following rollout.

Approvals
- Authorization path: Implementation requires signatures from plant maintenance management, operations management for line P3-L2, and quality engineering. The approval package will include a signed copy of this ECN, updated maintenance schedule entries for EQ-P3-L2-SB01, and evidence of personnel briefing.
- Post-implementation review: A coordinated review among maintenance, operations, and quality will be conducted after the initial monitoring period to verify that the shot media top-up practice yields the intended reduction in process variability. The review will reference the records described above and the governing SOPs SOP-P3-L2-02, SOP-P3-L2-03, and SOP-P3-L2-05 to ensure compliance.
- Document control: This ECN is Rev D and will be attached to the EQ-P3-L2-SB01 asset file and the revision history for the related SOPs where applicable. All relevant local work instructions will be updated to reflect the new top-up cadence and recordkeeping requirements.

Notes
- This change does not alter approved media specifications, part numbers, or the physical configuration of EQ-P3-L2-SB01. Any proposed variation beyond the scope of media top-up cadence must be addressed via a separate engineering change process.
